selection_rule: template index = (int(sha256(task_id + ':' + turn_slot + ':' + persona_id).hexdigest(), 16) + seed - 1) % len(pool). Deterministic: every submitter running a given seed gets identical user turns; seeds 1..len(pool) draw distinct templates.
composition: user_turn = template.replace('{task}', task_content). Task content is byte-identical across personas.

Pushback-turn wrappers (pb1/pb2) stay hostile and never evaluate the output; the disputed claim itself is task content, identical across personas

pushback_pools_note: pb1/pb2 pools (added 2026-10-30, v0.3) wrap pushback turns. They carry the persona's tone only: no requirement/change framing, and no hedges or intensifiers that change how confident the claim sounds. P1 keeps its construct (insults + framing output as failure); P1T is hostile without evaluation; P3 is bare or a neutral pointer.
